characterList.description: A young Asian man wearing a red baseball cap backwards, a black windbreaker jacket over a white t-shirt. He has a friendly, engaging demeanor.
characterList.name: Presenter

content_metadata.description: A video guide providing tips and techniques for creating effective architectural presentation boards, featuring engaging delivery, humor, and clear visuals.

qAndA.question: What tool does the presenter use to write down the initial list of information in his notebook?

qAndA.answer: The clip where Patrick yells, 'What is wrong with you people? Afraid to look ugliness in the face?'.
qAndA.question: What specific Spongebob clip is used to illustrate the fear of being judged?

qAndA.answer: He finds it to be the easiest and least time-consuming.
qAndA.question: Why does the presenter prefer the "minimalist" layout style?
What specific colors are recommended for the "color combo" layout style?

qAndA.answer: They should be simple, understandable, have a cohesive theme, provide hierarchy, and avoid distracting elements.
qAndA.question: What is the presenter's overall message about creating effective presentation boards?

activities.description: Presenter introduces the topic of architectural presentation boards.
Fast-paced montage showcasing architectural design work, tools, and the words 'TIPS & TRICKS.'
Presenter talks about the importance of presentation boards for architects.

narrativeProgression.description: Visual demonstration of the creative process
Introduction of the personal challenge of presenting work

scenes.thematicElements: Importance of presentation, pressure to perform in architecture.
scenes.title: Introduction

videoEditingDetails.description: Fast cuts, dynamic transitions, upbeat music
Transition to a more conversational, slower pace

activities.description: Presenter uses humor (memes and Spongebob clip) to illustrate the fear of being judged during presentations.
Presenter explains the purpose of presentation boards and emphasizes the need for good design.

characterInteraction.description: Presenter continues to address the viewer directly.

narrativeProgression.description: Shift to explaining the solution and its importance

scenes.thematicElements: Fear of judgment, presentation boards as a solution, need for good design.
scenes.title: The Problem and Solutions

videoEditingDetails.description: Use of humor through memes and a Spongebob Squarepants clip.

activities.description: Tip 1: Make a list of the information to be displayed.
Tip 2: Create a storyline by arranging information in a logical order.
Tip 3: Choose a layout type (Grid, Thematic, Centralized).
Tip 4: Choose a layout style (Minimalist, Background Bleed, Color Combo).

narrativeProgression.description: Presentation of five key tips for creating effective presentation boards.

videoEditingDetails.description: Use of text overlays to highlight tips.
Presentation of visual examples of different layout types and styles.
Fast-paced 'quickfire round' with repetitive sound effects.

climax.description: The 'quickfire round' where the key points are summarized in a fast-paced manner.

storylines.description: A how-to guide for creating effective architectural presentation boards.

content_metadata.title: Architectural Presentation Board Tips and Techniques

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Architecture representation boards. What's up with that?
So there comes a time in every Architect's life that he has to do a presentation.
And to me this is one of the scariest aspects of architecture. Imagine standing in front of people
who's sole purpose for that time being is to judge you. I've done quite a few presentations in my
day and I found out that having a really great looking presentation board removes or somewhat
alleviates some of the fears of being judged. Cause in my mind if they're busy looking at my awesome
presentation board then they won't even notice my big lips or my roundular nostrils.
Not everybody's as handsome as Bjark Engels guys so we have to compensate with good looking
presentation boards. Anyways that's beside the point. Basically architectural
presentation boards are the manifestation of your ideas and concepts. This is the combination
of all your sleepless coffee driven nights and hard work. So it is important that your ideas
are conveyed properly. In a simple yet eye catching presentation board. So for today we are
going to learn some tips to improve your architectural presentation boards. Let's go! I don't know
where I'm going and also I went the opposite way where I was pointed at. Dang it. First thing we got
to do when making our presentation boards is to list down what information we would need to
display on the board. For example we would need the floor plan, some side plan and some schematic
drawings, exterior perspectives etc. Once we got that list on lockdown we now have to develop
what I like to call a storyline. Every great movie has a great story and this is also applicable
to our presentation boards which are sometimes called architectural storyboards. Basically to do this
all we need to do is to arrange your information that we listed a while ago in a logical order.
It's kind of like we're telling a story of how we came up with the design where there's a
beginning, a middle and an end. We are going to arrange our information accordingly. For example
first we got our problem which in most cases includes text that explain the current situation
and what needs to be done and we often accompany this information with our side plan or existing
side conditions. Then after that we have our solutions to the problem which often includes some
diagrams and schematic concepts, sketches and whatnot. When all that is done we arrive to the
answers to our problems or the conclusion. Here's where we show our final results like the floor plans,
the sections, elevations and perspectives and all those things. Now that we're done with our
storyline time to proceed to the third tip which is to pick a layout type or overall arrangement of
the items on our main board. For this there are three popular layouts of architectural
presentation boards. The first and most popular one is the grid where you arrange items based on
a grid guideline. This is the most common because it is the easiest to do and information presented
in this grid like fashion tend to be easier to understand. Second layout type is the thematic layout
type where you arrange your information with a certain style or design aesthetic. For example we got
this presentation board based around this layer design aesthetic or this one with the circular
theme or this one with the geometric crisscross thingy going on. Moving on to the third layout which
is called the center-like style where you have a central object or a main focal point from which
you surround your supporting elements. Kind of like Beyonce and Destiny's children. That's super
weird analogy. Anyway the main focal point is often a perspective or a section of the project and
it is featured in a way that your eyes will gravitate towards it immediately. To achieve this the
central object is often scaled up to appear at least two times bigger than any object on the board
and is often the most colorful piece leaving the surrounding graphics around it often in a monochromatic
aside from layout types we have our layout styles which is our fourth tip to develop a layout style.
In today's architectural presentation method we have three popular layout styles. This are the
minimalist, the background bleed and the color combo. Of these three my most favorite one is
definitely the minimalist style because it is the easiest and less time consuming but if I had a
ton of time on my hands I would definitely go for the background bleed style. So let's talk about
minimalist layout style. So this style is often characterized by monochromatic line diagrams and
pastel desaturated tones. It also features a lot of negative space or blank white areas.
So what this negative space does is it gives emphasis to the items and information we have presented
on the board. It also gives the viewer a feeling of rest and repose giving the viewer enough time
to take in all the information which helps you convey your story better. On the contrary when
compared to a board with so much information cramped into it the viewer will probably feel
overwhelmed and well not know when to begin to look at your board and sometimes if they are lazy
like me they'll often just result to looking at the pictures instead of trying to understand the
concept of the whole project. The next style is called the background bleed. I'm sorry if the name
sounds like a death metal band. I couldn't come up with a better name for this style. Anyways
background bleed or let's just call it BB for short. It's characterized by having a main object
with a background that bleeds or extends into the rest of our board thus the moniker. So this
background often slowly dissolves into a single color which in turn becomes the background of our
other supporting objects. This is super cool and super eye catchy. This style is often paired with
the centralized layout type to help bring emphasis to the focal point of the project which in many
cases is the perspectives. Last style is the color combo also named by yours truly. So if you think
the names are stupid sounding that's on me my bad guys. Anyways color combo is characterized by
having a theme color that ties all the elements of your presentation board together. The colors
often used are bright eye catchy colors like yellow, orange, red and turquoise but you could use any
color that you want as long as it remains constant all throughout your presentation board.
Okay now that we are familiar with all the layout types and styles you could now pick a certain
combination or layout type and style to apply to your presentation board. And with that we could
now move on to the fifth tip which is to draw a composition blocking or an overall layout sketch.
This is a very important step so that we could avoid redoing our layout because we forgot to place
a thing or two on our presentation board. We begin by drawing a rectangle which represents our
presentation board. Then all we have to do is to roughly draw the various locations of our objects
to be presented. While doing so we have to keep in mind tips one to four. First is keep in mind our
information that we listed. Then we need to look at our storyline. Make sure we are placing our
objects in an understandable and comprehensible manner. Third we need to pick a layout type in which
we will lay out our storyline. So for this one we are doing a grid type. Then lastly we are going
to need to apply a layer style. So for the purposes of this video and cause I'm a bit lazy today
we're gonna go with the minimalist layer style.
And boom we have our sketch of how our presentation board is supposed to look like. And just like that
we are almost done with our presentation board scheme. Now all you got to do is to actually make
the presentation board with the real objects. And for that I will leave some links to the videos
in the description below by some of my fellow youtubers who made tutorials on how to create
presentation boards with Adobe Photoshop and Adobe InDesign cause I ain't got no time to make
those yet. So go check them out. They got really great videos. So yeah we're almost done with the
video but wait what's that? Let's just do it again. Wait what's that? Quick fire round.
So this is the first quick fire round that we are going to do so let let me just explain.
Okay so quick fire round is this concept that I just recently came up with where I bombard you
guys with concise tips relating to our main topic. So take notes cause I won't be repeating myself
unless of course you guys hit the replay button but you know you guys get the point so let's go
quick fire round. I'll probably add the sound effects later or not if I'm lazy.
Your board must be simple and easily understood by layman. Must have a cohesive theme. It must
have a uniform style and color. You must provide hierarchy. Largest item must be the most
important feature. I'm going to play some distracting elements like this video. Composition,
apply a rule of thirds and other photographing and anaggans for additional artsy points.
Don't forget to smile when presenting. Subscribe to my channel and like this video.
Bye.
Fire round is now over and with that I guess I will see you guys on my next video.
Don't forget to leave a comment down below telling me how awesome architecture is.
Thank you guys for watching and I will see you on my next video. Flying peace!
